chunks: And with this chain of narration, he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
When you eat tharid (bread soaked in broth), eat from the sides of the dish, for the blessing is in the middle.

key_terms.الثَّرِيدُ: A dish made of bread soaked in meat broth or soup
key_terms.الذُّرْوَةُ: The top, peak, or middle part (often considered the best part)

ai.seo_question: Where is the blessing located when eating tharid according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights the Prophetic practice of distributing food with humility, where the 'middle' (al-dhurwa) represents the prime portion or the locus of divine blessing. In Shia scholarly tradition, this is often interpreted as a lesson in modesty and generosity, encouraging the eater to leave the best part for others or to consume it with gratitude, thereby inviting more barakah into the meal.
